The split makes GCC allocate the shifted value in $a0 to match the target (`srl $a0,$v0,8; ...; andi $a0,$a0,1`); the single expression puts it in $v1 and loses 10 points. Full body: `u32 v=func_8000DB70(); s32 bit; bit=v>>8; bit&=1; if(v&0x80) *(s32*)(arg0+4)=(*(s32*)(arg0+4)|bit)&~2; return bit;`

Match requires the absolute MMIO address, not an extern symbol: `if (!(*(volatile u32 *)0xA4040010 & 1)) return -1; *(volatile u32 *)0xA4080000 = arg0; return 0;`. With `extern u32 D_A4080000;` GCC emitted the `lui $at / sw %lo(D_A4080000)($at)` form (at-based) and the wrong branch layout; the absolute constant produces `lui $v0,%hi(addr); sw %lo(addr)($v0)` in the beqz delay slot, which is what the ROM has. MATCHED (byte-identical, 38 insns) after 1195 -> 160 -> 0. Pure constant-store init function; the whole game is about where the compiler materializes the two shared constants (0x180 reused 10x, 0x380 reused 4x) and in which register. Key: the target materializes 0x180 early (addiu v1,0x180 at insn 8, right after addiu v0,0x1E4 and before its store) and 0x380 later (addiu v0,0x380), even though the STORES using 0x180 happen ~14 insns later. Plain m2c order with literals (or s16/s32 local variables assigned at their natural place) scores 1195: this build keeps 0x180's addiu next to its first use and gives it v0 instead of v1. Fix: declare `s16 h; s16 w;`, assign `h = 0x180;` right after the `0x28A = 0x1E4` store, and put the first h-using store (`0x132=0;` then `0x12C=h; 0x136=h; 0x12E=h; 0x138=h;`) immediately after it — closeness of the first use makes the compiler keep one early materialization (v1, since v0 holds 0x1E4 at that point), and the scheduler delays the actual stores to their ROM positions. Then `w = 0x380;` after the `0x174=0x70` store, and keep the tail stores in the ROM order (0x152=0; 0x14C..0x158 group; 0x172=0; 0x16C/0x176/0x17A/0x16E/0x178). That got 160; the last 160->0 was setting the source store order to exactly the ROM store order in the tail (0x132 zero before the 0x12C group, 0x14C group before the 0x172 zero). So: constants' addiu position follows the source position of their first use, while stores are delayed by sched1 to ROM order — source order need not equal final store order.

KEY FINDING on the saved-register mapping (also applies to the identical sibling func_801662E8_ovl_16). Target wants s0=a, s1=const1, s2=b, s3=c. The const 1 must be a source local (`s32 one = 1;`) used in the switch compare and `a->unk7 = one;`. With just that, KMC assigns one->s3, b->s1, c->s2 (score 505). GCC global-alloc ranks by ref count: one needs ONE MORE surviving ref than b/c to win s1. Crucially, cse/combine constant-folds a use of `one` when it occurs BEFORE the first call in a block (e.g. `a->unk1E0 = one+99` folds to addiu zero,100; `a->unk6 += one` folds to addiu ...,1; `a->unk7 = one+2` in case 2 folds), so those add no ref. A use AFTER a call survives: `a->unk2CE = one + 2` in case 3 gives the correct s1=one/s2=b/s3=c mapping (score 445, 96.5%) but emits `addiu v0,s1,2` instead of the target's `addiu v1,zero,3`. Likewise `if (n == one+3)` post-call gives mapping s1 but `addiu v0,s1,3` vs target `addiu v0,zero,4` (score 450), and `n = a->unk1F4 + one` gives `addu a0,a0,s1` vs target `addiu a0,a0,1` (score 640). What is still needed: a post-call use of `one` that reload rematerializes back to the target's zero-based immediate, so the ref survives alloc but emits identical code. Remaining diffs besides that operand are scheduling: `lbu 0x2CB` is hoisted before `move a0,s0` in ours; `addiu a1,s0,0x1E0` placement; `lh a1,0x66(v0)` vs after `move a0,s0`; `lhu v0,0x2C8` hoisted before `lui v1,0xA00`; case1 second block uses v0/v1 swapped for 0x2C4/0x32; case2 0x5000F00 uses v0/v1 swapped; case3 target keeps `a` in a0 for the body (lbu 0x26F(a0), sb 0x2CE(a0)) while ours uses s0.
